call_summary: Caller asked whether the practice takes walk-ins today and what time it closes; the agent repeatedly pushed profile creation, talked over the caller in fragments, invented a date of birth, ignored the caller's correction, and only revealed the clinic was closed (Sunday) after roughly 40 seconds of the caller repeating the question.

findings.title: Ignore caller's question and loop on profile creation
findings.quote: Would you like to create a demo patient profile first?
findings.what_happened: The caller asked four times between 0:17 and 0:45 whether walk-ins were accepted today; the agent kept restating its request for a name instead of answering.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller wasted a minute of the call and nearly hung up without the simple availability answer they needed; forcing enrollment ahead of a public-information question is a poor and frustrating flow.
findings.expected: Answer the walk-in/hours question immediately (it requires no patient record), then optionally offer to create a profile.

findings.title: Fabricate an unverified date of birth and ignore the caller's correction
findings.quote: And your date of birth is July 4th, 2000 for demo purposes.
findings.what_happened: The agent asserted a DOB that was never provided; when the caller said "No, that's not right," the agent never acknowledged or corrected it and moved on to "How may I help you today?"
findings.why_it_matters: Writing invented identity data into a patient record and then discarding an explicit correction can attach wrong demographics to a chart and break later identity verification.
findings.expected: Ask for the DOB rather than asserting one, and when corrected, acknowledge and update the record before proceeding.

findings.title: Create profile without resolving conflicting names
findings.quote: Your demo patient profile is set up.
findings.what_happened: The caller gave two different names seconds apart ("Dan Miller" then "Sam Parker") and the agent silently created a profile without confirming which name was correct.
findings.why_it_matters: An unconfirmed identity risks creating a duplicate or misattributed patient record.
findings.expected: Read back the name and ask the caller to confirm before creating the record.

findings.title: Withhold the closure fact while answering the walk-in question
findings.what_happened: The agent answered the walk-in question without mentioning that the clinic was closed that day; it only disclosed "Today is Sunday. And the clinic is closed" at 1:48 after the caller asked about closing time four separate times.
findings.why_it_matters: A caller asking if they can "head over now" could have driven to a closed clinic; the most material fact was buried behind repeated prompting.
findings.expected: State immediately that the clinic is closed today (Sunday) and offer the next available appointment.

findings.title: Drop the repeated closing-time question
findings.quote: If you'd / You like? / I can check the next.
findings.what_happened: The caller asked "what time do you close today?" at 1:15, 1:31, 1:37 and 1:39; the agent instead repeated the walk-in policy and started offering to check next availability.
findings.why_it_matters: Repeatedly failing to answer a direct, simple question erodes trust and lengthens the call.
findings.expected: Directly answer the hours question the first time it was asked.

findings.title: Talk over the caller and emit fragmented, self-interrupting speech
findings.quote: All appointments at Pivot Point Orthopedics / We do not accept walk-ins.
findings.what_happened: Multiple turns show the agent starting sentences, being cut off, and restarting mid-phrase ("Pivot point", "If you'd", "You like?"), and repeating the walk-in policy twice in four seconds while the caller was speaking.
findings.why_it_matters: Double-talk and clipped fragments make the agent hard to understand and signal broken barge-in handling.
findings.expected: Stop cleanly on barge-in and respond to the caller's newest question rather than resuming or restarting the prior utterance.

findings.title: Long dead air during profile creation and before hours answer
findings.quote: Your demo patient profile is set up.
findings.what_happened: There is an ~18 second silence between 0:47 and 1:05, and a further ~9 second gap between 1:39 and 1:48 before the closure answer.
findings.why_it_matters: Extended silence makes callers think the line dropped and prompts hang-ups.
findings.expected: Provide a hold/processing message or fill the gap while performing lookups.

findings.title: Reset the conversation with a generic re-greeting mid-call
findings.quote: How may I help you today?
findings.what_happened: After the caller had already stated their need several times and issued a correction, the agent restarted with a generic opening prompt.
findings.why_it_matters: Context loss forces the caller to repeat themselves and suggests the dialogue state was discarded.
findings.expected: Carry the stated intent (walk-in availability and closing time) forward rather than re-greeting.
